# DS Business Analyst Case (P&L Decomposition)

[← Capital One](../README.md) · [Every Capital One question](../../capital-one.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/ds-business-analyst-case-study)

`critical-thinking` `math-reasoning` `open-ended` `verbal`

---

## Requirements

- The interviewer gives you a specific business situation involving credit or lending. Examples that have been reported include:
  - Should credit-line increases be extended to a particular customer group? Estimate the effects on revenue and defaults.
  - A credit product is being introduced in a new geographic market — evaluate its likely profitability.
  - A revision to a risk model has been suggested — how would it affect P&L sensitivity?
- Phase 1: establish the objective — higher revenue, fewer defaults, or greater overall profit?
- Phase 2: break the problem into a P&L formula: `Profit = Revenue - Loss - Operational Cost`. In credit products, revenue can come from interest income, interchange, and fees, while losses include charge-offs and provisions.
- Phase 3: determine the relevant drivers — interest rate, credit limit, risk-model threshold, and segment definition.
- Phase 4: use mental math to test sensitivity around the most influential driver.

## Notes

- **Do not begin with modelling.** The most frequent mistake in this round is hearing “DS interview” and proposing an XGBoost solution within the opening two minutes. The evaluation emphasizes business decomposition first; modelling may come much later, if it appears at all.
- Credit-lending P&L analysis follows a particular structure worth committing to memory: `Profit = (APR × Balance × Approval Rate − Charge-off Rate × Balance × Approval Rate − Operating Cost per Account) × Population`. This template allows the candidate to separate a new scenario into its four levers in a consistent way.
- Mental math: answers should be roughly estimated but accurate. A 5% charge-off rate applied to $1B of balances produces a $50M loss; adding $100M of balance from a newly recruited segment with an 8% charge-off rate creates an $8M incremental loss. Rehearse calculations of this size and simplicity.
- The later role-play and BQ stages assess the same business framing when communicating with a PM — the case and role-play stages are evaluated together.

## Preparation

- Commit the credit-product P&L template above to memory. Apply it to three situations — a line increase, a new geographic market, and a risk-model change — until the breakdown becomes automatic.
- Train with credit-product reference calculations: $1B in balance × 18% APR equals $180M in revenue; a 5% charge-off rate × $1B equals a $50M loss. Reach the result within 30 seconds.
- Build the discipline of *not modelling*. If the interviewer brings up data, first state the dependent variable plainly (“the model would predict default probability for each account”) before talking about features or algorithms — this shows that you recognize modelling is part of the process but is not the focus of this round.
